name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Andrea Salinas is an incumbent in a D+6 district with about $1.9 million raised and $646,000 on hand
Republican David Russ has raised only about $13,000 with $21 on hand, showing no visible campaign
No outside spending opposes Salinas, and prediction markets price Democrats near 97 percent
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: Salinas holds a six-point Democratic district, enjoys a roughly 150-to-1 fundraising advantage, faces no outside opposition spending, and markets give her about a 97 percent win probability. With no polling or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the seat stays firmly in the Safe Democratic column.
model.watch: The race could tighten only through an unexpected late wave of outside spending against Salinas or an unforeseen scandal, neither of which is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's sixth district leans Democratic by six points, and incumbent Andrea Salinas is seeking re-election with the full advantages of incumbency. She has raised about $1.9 million and holds roughly $646,000 on hand. Her Republican opponent, David Russ, has raised about $13,000 and reports just $21 in cash, leaving little sign of a competitive campaign. No outside groups have spent against Salinas, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat.

No public general-election polls are available, so expectations rest on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. All of those signals point the same way toward a comfortable Democratic hold, with an expected Democratic margin near twenty points and the race rated Safe Democratic.
